problem.title: How many clients are you losing because your messages reach no one?

items.title: Cold emails don't get opened anymore
items.text: You send fifty, you get zero replies. Between spam filters, crowded inboxes and messages that smell like a template, cold email keeps hitting a lower ceiling.

items.title: People do answer the phone — but it's daunting
items.text: They pick up, and you have no idea what they do, where to start or how to handle a "not interested". That's how people quit calling after the third try.

items.title: Finding companies by hand eats your week
items.text: Google, each company's website, copying the phone number into a spreadsheet. Hours of mechanical work before you've spoken to a single person.

items.q: How long until I see results?
items.a: Your first list is ready in under 5 minutes and you can start calling the same day. Unlike email, a call tells you straight away whether there's interest: you don't wait days for a reply that rarely comes.

Two reasons. Coverage: almost every company publishes a phone number and far fewer a usable contact email. And in Spain the law is much clearer about B2B phone calls than about cold email. We still include AI emails, but the phone is the channel we recommend.

We don't run technical mailbox verification (SMTP or MX). We extract the emails companies publish on their own websites, so they are real, public addresses, but they may be outdated or generic inboxes. We'd rather be straight with you: if you need delivery guarantees, the phone is the reliable route.

items.q: Is cold calling businesses legal in Spain?
items.a: Business-to-business calling has a much clearer legal footing than cold email. Spain's LSSI requires prior consent or an existing contractual relationship for commercial email, even B2B — something many tools gloss over. That said, this isn't legal advice: check your specific case, and always respect opt-out lists and any request not to be called again.

items.q: What if I don't know what to say on the phone?
items.a: That's what the call brief is for. Before you dial you have what the company does, why calling them makes sense, the exact opening line, three questions to find out whether they're a fit and prepared answers to the usual objections.

items.q: How is this different from Hunter.io or Apollo?
items.a: Hunter and Apollo are contact databases built for the English-speaking market and for email. OpenSells is built for Spain, in Spanish, and doesn't stop at handing you data: it prepares the conversation. The value isn't the list, it's knowing what to say when they pick up.

Yes, no lock-in and no penalties. Cancel from your dashboard in 30 seconds and you won't be charged the following month. And if you cancel within the first 7 days we refund you in full, no questions asked.

items.q: Does it work for any industry?
items.a: It works especially well when selling to businesses with premises and a visible phone number: repair shops, clinics, consultancies, accountants, hospitality, training, real estate. If your client is a company you can call, OpenSells is for you.
